questions.enonce_markdown: Given that $f=\dfrac{uv}{u-v}$, express $u$ in terms of $f$ and $v$. *[5 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The letter $u$ appears twice, so collect all the terms in $u$ on one side.

Multiply both sides by $(u-v)$: $f(u-v)=uv$.

Expand: $fu-fv=uv$.

Move the terms in $u$ to the left: $fu-uv=fv$.

Factorise: $u(f-v)=fv$.

Divide by $(f-v)$: $u=\dfrac{fv}{f-v}$.

Check with $u=6$, $v=3$: $f=\dfrac{18}{3}=6$, and $\dfrac{fv}{f-v}=\dfrac{18}{3}=6$.

**Answer: $u=\dfrac{fv}{f-v}$.**
